assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Lifted toward the company's own plan and stated capacity (round-1 review C4). The Company is "targeting the coal production at the higher end of the range of between 39-76 million MT" for 2026 [S6, F47] and is ramping Tabang "to more than 80 million MT per annum" [S6, F33] on the US$0.77bn of debottlenecking capex already spent [S6, F34]. FY2026E is RESET to 65 Mt by the nine-month result (30 Oct 2026) and re-keyed on the correct S8 columns (review C12): the two disclosed 2026 quarters sold 15.0 Mt (1Q26, F48) and 15.8 Mt (2Q26, F74), a 30.8 Mt first half; nine-month revenue of US$2,434.2m [S21, F49] less the 1H26 revenue in the same S8 table leaves a third quarter compressed by the September RKAB force-majeure halt [S13, S14]. The fourth quarter then carries the seasonal recovery at close to the 80 Mtpa nameplate — about 20 Mt a quarter — and the 67.2 Mt committed and contracted book dated end-July [S8, F14] plus the additional 15-20 Mt of ESDM quota [F45, F46, S14] support it. That lands the full year at 65 Mt: below the 67.2 Mt book because the shutdown is not fully recoverable, and well below the 76 Mt production ceiling. The 65 Mt is below the FY2025 actual of 70.8 Mt [F1] — the reported outcome of a permit-stoppage year, not a haircut. We then grow back into the funded capacity — FY2027E 77, FY2028E 80 — and HOLD FLAT at 80 Mt rather than fading: the RKAB additional quota of 15-20 Mt ESDM granted the three subsidiaries [F45, F46], the stated JORC reserve base [F8] and the committed book [F14] support the resumption, nothing in the reserve statement sources a decline, and the most-likely policy forbids an unsourced volume fade — but the FY2027E lift is a plan, stated as such, after a 2026 that missed its own guide. The path is capped by JORC reserves in the engine [F8].

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Bayan realises a deep discount to the Newcastle 6,000 NAR marker: its product is lower-CV sub-bituminous (the 2026 contracted book is priced at an average of 4,088 kcal/kg GAR, S8/F18), a quarter of tonnes go to the domestic market at HBA/DMO-linked prices (25.7% of volume in 2025, F10), and the method card is explicit that Indonesian coal realisation keys off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle. The ratio is calibrated on the LAST completed fiscal year's actuals against the deck series that carries a forward path, d.coal.newc: FY2025 ASP of US$48.4/MT (F3) over the deck's FY2025A average of US$108.4/MT [d.coal.newc] = 0.446, corroborated by FY2024 at 0.450 (ASP US$61.3/MT, F4, over US$136.1/MT). GRADE CORROBORATION (round-1 review C3): the ratio is the arithmetic of Bayan's grade, not a company haircut. The coal deck's own reviewed government prints show HBA II at 4,100 kcal/kg GAR — the grade BYAN's 4,088 GAR book sits on — at US$66.10/t spot against Newcastle spot US$150.35/t, a ratio of 0.44 that is essentially identical to BYAN's calibrated 0.446 [coal deck hba_ii & newc spots, both reviewed]; the covered peer AADI realises 0.63 on the same Newcastle marker because its Envirocoal is a 4,000-5,000 kcal ultra-low-pollutant product clearing nearer the HBA I (5,300 GAR, US$93.62/t spot) level, 93.62/150.35 = 0.62 [coal deck hba_i spot, reviewed]. The ~18pp gap to AADI is therefore GRADE, and the model uses the grade-matched HBA II print as CORROBORATION rather than as the driver, because the reviewed HBA forward series is high-GAR (6,322 kcal/kg) and the grade-matched HBA II has spot prints only, with no forecast path. From FY2027E out the ratio is held flat rather than drifted, because a ratio fitted to a forecast year would carry that year's premium or trough into the long run — which is exactly the error the restated FY2025A deck actual now removes. FY2026E IS THE EXCEPTION, and it is set from actuals, not from a forecast: nine months of 2026 revenue of US$2,434.2m [S21, F49] with disclosed quarterly ASPs of US$48.7/t in 1Q26 and US$58.1/t in 2Q26 [S8, F75, F70] shows Bayan's realised price near the half-year average, not at the US$61/t that 0.4465 x the deck's FY2026E Newcastle marker would produce. The realised-to-marker ratio for 2026 is therefore about 0.40: the war-premium spike in the high-CV Newcastle marker is not being captured in a 4,088 kcal/kg book, which is the same point the HBA II corroboration makes (0.44 at the spot prints). The year is set at 0.40 and the through-cycle years stay at 0.4465, so the 2026 print does not leak into the long-run value.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Near a quarter of Bayan's tonnes go to the Indonesian domestic market (25.7% of volume in 2025, F10) and the Tabang operations meet their Domestic Market Obligation in kind while the higher-CV mines pay DMO compensation, so we place 25% of tonnes under the standing US$70/t power cap carried in the coal deck (d.coal.dmo_cap). Capped tonnes receive min(cap, realised price), and on the current deck the cap never binds in the base or the bull case: the grade-adjusted realisation times the deck's near-year benchmark stays below the cap, so min() returns the realised price and the capped share is a tail guard that would bite only on a sustained benchmark spike toward the reviewed spot (round-2 QC Q10) [S0]. Why 25% is a level and not a rising ceiling: the DMO is a fixed share of output set by the government (25% of production for domestic supply), and the company's own disclosed domestic share has been stable at 25.7% of volume in the last full year [F10], so we hold the capped share at 25% rather than ramp it. The government is constraining total output through RKAB quotas, not lifting the DMO percentage, so a rising domestic share is a risk we state in §5 rather than a modelled drift.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Cost intensity is carried as a unit factor rather than a physical bcm/t ratio: the reported cost stack is per-tonne, so the mined ratio (group strip ratio 4.5x based on production volume in 2025, 4.7x in 2Q26, F7) is used as the physical context and the factor below is the per-tonne cost intensity that reproduces the reported unit cost. It drifts up modestly as Tabang's stripping rises off its current low base (Tabang at 3.9x in 2025 against a 4.5x mine plan) and the short-haul coal is exhausted. PEER-COMPARABILITY RECONCILIATION (the AADI/GEMS/BUMI convention books the physical bcm/t ratio in this axis with a cost_per_bcm of US$2.6-8.0/t, so BYAN's unit factor 1.0 is NOT directly comparable): here unit_factor = 1.0 and the axis is a cost-intensity multiplier, so strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm = 1.0 x US$22.0/t is the mining-block cost per tonne, which equals the peer-implied mining cost per tonne (AADI 4.35 bcm/t x US$4.3/t ≈ US$18.7/t; BUMI 8.0 x US$2.6 ≈ US$20.8/t) once BYAN's self-operated logistics and lower physical ratio are allowed for — i.e. the per-tonne cash cost is the comparable quantity, not the axis value. The group's physical strip ratio of 4.5x [F7] is disclosed as context in §1 and §3.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Mining cost per tonne ex-royalty. Backed out of the reported cash cost and the presentation's own 2Q26 cost stack (overburden and mining 39%, coal hauling 19%, barging 13%, employee 9%, other production 6%, SGA 2%, royalty 12% of a US$37.0/MT all-in cost, S8): ex-royalty cash cost of about US$32.6/MT at 2Q26 and US$28.6/MT at the FY2025 all-in cost of US$32.5/MT (F5), with the nine-month run-rate (COGS less royalty and D&A over disclosed 2026 sales) near US$30/MT. We carry the 2026 run-rate — US$29.5/MT ex-royalty — in FY2026E, because 65 Mt is below the 70.8 Mt FY2025 volume and the company itself attributes part of the 2Q26 unit-cost rise to "Lower sales volumes which negatively impacts various unit costs" [S8; review C14]. As volume returns to the 80 Mt capacity the unit cost reverts toward the FY2025 full-volume level (US$28.6/MT), which is why the factor steps DOWN from FY2026E to FY2028E before resuming nominal escalation; the decline is the volume normalisation S8 describes, not an unsourced efficiency gain. It then drifts up moderately as Tabang's stripping rises off a low base. Fuel is passed through the deck's Brent path.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Residual per-tonne cost after the royalty and the mining block: employee, other production, SGA and contingency, plus the small non-coal cost base. Set so that the modelled FY2026E unit cost plus royalty lines up with the FY2025 realised all-in cash cost of US$32.5/MT (F5) and the 1H26 run-rate, and inflated gently with wage and services cost thereafter. This is where the barging, employee and SGA shares of the 2Q26 cost stack sit, so it is larger than the mining block per tonne at Tabang's current stripping.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK notes, not the data pack: Bayan's consolidated fixed-asset depreciation is US$111.1m for FY2025 (F22) and US$96.6m for FY2024 (F23) per the segment note, i.e. US$1.57/t on FY2025 sales of 70.8 Mt (and US$1.72/t on FY2024's 56.2 Mt) — the pack's US$2.0m D&A is a stub because the IDX cash-flow statement uses the direct method and carries no D&A add-back. Mining- property amortisation (US$10.5m FY2025, US$6.4m FY2024) is not added separately: it is already inside the reported cash cost the unit-cost build reconciles to, so counting it here would double-count. Held at the FY2025A rate of US$1.57/t thereafter, with the fleet contracted and expensed through the cash-cost line.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Sustaining capex only. Bayan guided 2026 capex to US$200-300 million (S6) against FY2025 capex of about US$171m (S0), which on ~71 Mt is roughly US$3/t; part of that is discretionary growth (the fourth Muara Pahu barge loader, BCT upgrade) and is carried separately in capex_other, so the per-tonne sustaining figure is set below the guided average. Held FLAT in real terms thereafter — the series escalates with the macro deck's US long-run inflation, so there is no real drift; the most-likely policy holds costs at the last actual in real terms and nothing in the filings sources a real rise in sustaining capex per tonne.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Discretionary expansion capex, the balance of the guided US$200-300m 2026 programme (S6): the fourth barge loader at Muara Pahu and the BCT and FSP camp works. Held near the guided run-rate for the first three years, then stepped down as the Tabang capacity programme completes; the buoyant case in §4 adds nothing here because the capacity is already funded.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Payout is the company's own five-year record: 73% of NPAT for 2021-2025 (F12), with US$700m paid in respect of 2024 and US$500m in respect of 2025 (F11) against a net-cash balance sheet and no debt. We hold 73% rather than the engine's three-year average, which is skewed by the extraordinary FY2022-FY2023 cycle, and treat the dividend as the anchor the market prices. The latest year's ratio is lower than the record — the US$500m distribution is a smaller share of FY2025 parent profit than the five-year average — because the board sets the distribution in absolute dollars and has held it roughly flat as earnings came off the FY2022 peak, rather than targeting a fixed ratio (round-2 QC Q7) [S8, F11, F12]. The five-year record, not the latest year, is therefore the most likely forward payout: it is what the board has actually delivered across a full price cycle, and a single year in which earnings rose faster than the absolute dividend is the least representative observation in the sample.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary DCF runs to the end of the reserve life with no terminal value, so this input only feeds the cross-checks (EV/EBITDA and the implied multiple frame). It is set at the house cap for a USD-reporting name, below long-run US inflation, because a thermal-coal cash flow stream should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Bayan runs a lean corporate cost base: SG&A has averaged under 3% of revenue over FY2023-FY2025 in the data pack (S0). Held near the historical average, drifting up slightly as corporate and ESG costs grow.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Effective royalty of 8% of revenue, derived bottom-up from the Company's own disclosed cost stack rather than from the IUPK parent rate: in the 2Q26 presentation royalty is 12% of a US$37.0/MT all-in cash cost (US$4.4/MT) against a US$58.1/MT ASP, i.e. 7.6% of revenue, and the same arithmetic on FY2025 (12% of US$32.5/MT on a US$48.4/MT ASP) gives 8.1% (S8, F5). We use a flat 8% because Bayan is not an ex-PKP2B IUPK converter and so sits outside the IUPK step schedule, and the presentation states its rates are "lower royalty rates than IUPK's" (S8). The 2025 royalty regime change (PP 18/2025, PP 19/2025) is a live policy risk carried in §5. The deck's reviewed IUPK step table (coal.royalty_iupk) applies only to ex-PKP2B continuation holders (KPC, Arutmin, Berau, MHU, Kendilo, AADI) and so is not read for Bayan; the deck's IUP calorie table (coal.royalty_iup) is needs_source, so the regime cannot be tilted against Bayan on that basis. Double-count check: royalty is already INSIDE the reported US$32.5/MT cash cost (F5's label reads "incl. royalty"), so the mining block and other_cost_unit are set EX-ROYALTY (cost_per_bcm 22.0 + other_cost_unit 5.5 = US$27.5/MT, against the ex-royalty US$28.6/MT implied by stripping 12% of US$32.5), and the engine adds royalty back as a separate % of revenue — so the line is counted once, not twice.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Fuel is a real cost pressure — the Company named higher fuel prices as the main driver of the 2Q26 cash-cost increase (S8) — but most of Bayan's mining, hauling and barging is contracted to third parties at unit rates that already embed their diesel cost, so only a minority of the cost base is directly fuel-exposed. We set 10% rather than the 30% template convention, and give the reason: the oil deck's long-run Brent is a seeded, war-premium value, and passing a perpetual war premium through the mining cost while the coal deck mean-reverts toward US$105/t would manufacture a margin squeeze that neither deck actually asserts.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Non-coal revenue (the small oil-palm and services lines) was about US$20m in 2025 (S6); carried flat rather than grown, as it is immaterial to value.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Template constant 10%; the non-coal lines are immaterial to group value.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The group remains in NET CASH, but it is no longer debt-free: the 30 Sep 2026 LK carries US$148.6m of short-term bank loans (nil at 31 Dec 2025), split between PT Bank Mega and BCA per the borrowings note, against US$769.0m of cash, so net cash is US$620.4m [S21, F64, F63]. The nine-month cash-flow shows US$280m of short-term bank loans drawn and US$130m repaid [S21, F77]. This input is NET NEW borrowing across the forecast, not the existing balance, which the engine already carries in its history and bridge; we assume no further net drawdown because the balance sheet stays in net cash and the dividend is covered [S21]. Review C17 asks for the terms and the finding is carried in sections five and six.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Bayan's non-operating line is dominated by interest income on its net-cash balance, which the engine computes separately via cash_yield; no separate non-operating items assumed.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count is fixed at the reported 33,333,335,000 shares; no issuance or buyback assumed. The October 2026 block transfer moved ownership between existing holders and changes no share count (S10).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Engine default carried from history: the three-year average of net working capital over revenue in the data pack (S0). Bayan runs a negative-to-thin working-capital position because coal is largely pre-sold, so this is a small drag and is held flat.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Engine default carried from history: the three-year average effective tax rate in the data pack (S0), close to the 22% Indonesian statutory rate. Held flat; a lower realised price would not change the statutory rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Bayan carries only US$148.6m of short-term bank loans against US$769.0m of cash [S21, F64, F63], so the cost of debt is not a value driver; the engine default from the thin historical interest expense line is carried unchanged.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history (S0). Cross-checked against the disclosed treasury holdings: Bayan subscribed IDR3tn (US$180m) of Patriot Bonds at a 2% coupon in October 2025 and holds a large net-cash balance (S8), so a low-single-digit yield is consistent.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history (S0): minority interests take a small low-single-digit share of net profit, consistent with the reported minority balance sheet interest.

challenges.challenge: The report names the pending change of control as a floor but never prices it. On completion POJK 9/2018 requires a mandatory tender offer struck at the highest of the reference price and the prior-90-day average - and the deal price (Rp2,588) is far below the tape while the 90-day average is near it, so the tender price would land near or ABOVE today's Rp10,475 and well above our Rp7,836 target. A floor above the target makes the REDUCE's -20.1% expected return wrong on a risk-adjusted basis.
challenges.answer: Now priced, not only named. A completed change of control would trigger a POJK 9/2018 mandatory tender struck at the higher of the deal price (F15, Rp2,588) and the prior-ninety-day market reference; the transfer-era prints — F16 close Rp11,100 on the 15 Oct transfer, F17 on-market purchase at Rp11,200 on 14 Oct — place the ninety-day reference ABOVE today's close and above our target, so a completed tender floors the exit above the target. We hold that as a dated, PROBABILISTIC catalyst rather than the base, because the company states no change of control has occurred (F20 Low+Elaine 30.30% > F13 Jhonlin 30.25%; no POJK 9/2018 takeover announcement) — the conditions precedent, and the completion probability, are captured in the konglo lens's bull regime weight rather than assumed away. §4 prices the floor and the frontmatter carries it as a dated catalyst.

challenges.challenge: The konglo registry (fund record show) states the 16 Sep 2026 SPA is 'not yet completed', and the report frames the whole control transfer as pending. But F13/S10 show PT Jhonlin Baratama ALREADY holds 10,084,088,370 shares = 30.25% as at the October ownership report, with Low Tuck Kwong at 8.3% (F19) and he plus Elaine Low at 30.30% (F20). If the block has already moved, the tender-offer trigger and the registry's 'pending' status are inconsistent.
challenges.answer: Reconciled, and the reconciliation is the finding: the SHARES moved, CONTROL did not. The block transferred — PT Jhonlin Baratama held nothing in the 31 Mar 2026 shareholder list (S5) but holds F13 (30.25%) at the 19 Oct 2026 ownership report, and Low Tuck Kwong fell to F19 (S10). Control did not change: Dato' Low Tuck Kwong and Elaine Low still hold F20 (30.30%) together, marginally above Jhonlin, and the company states on the basis of their 8 Oct 2026 control letters and the absence of any POJK 9/2018 takeover announcement that it has received nothing showing a change of control [S10]. So the 30.25% holding, the exchange's clarification and the registry's 'not yet completed' are all consistent: the conditional SPA's block transferred, but the formal change of control — and with it the tender obligation — has NOT been triggered. §6 rewritten to distinguish the two.

challenges.challenge: The model prices the name at d.coal.newc x0.447 while the method card keys Indonesian coal off HBA/ICI and the deck carries a REVIEWED d.coal.hba FY2027E 112.0 (spot 126.81). The covered peer AADI uses realisation 0.63 on the same Newcastle marker with the same 0.25 capped share, so the DMO share does not explain a ~18pp gap - only grade does. A peer-consistent realisation would raise the DCF materially.
challenges.answer: Bridged on GRADE. The ratio is calibrated on the last actual (FY2025 ASP F3 US$48.4 over the deck's FY2025A Newcastle 108.4 = 0.446, corroborated by FY2024 F4 61.3/136.1 = 0.450), never on a forecast spike. The gap to AADI is grade, shown from the coal deck's OWN reviewed prints: HBA II (4,100 kcal/kg GAR) — the grade BYAN's book sits on (F18 4,088 GAR) — clears at US$66.10/t against a Newcastle spot of US$150.35/t, a ratio of 0.44 essentially equal to ours, while AADI's higher-CV ultra-low-pollutant Envirocoal clears nearer HBA I (5,300 GAR, US$93.62/t), 0.62, matching AADI's 0.63. On why the reviewed HBA marker is not the anchor: the HBA FORWARD series is high-GAR (6,322 kcal/kg), well above this grade, and the grade-matched HBA II has spot prints only — no forecast path — so the only reviewed series that can carry a through-cycle DCF is newc, with the grade-calibrated ratio. Now stated in §1 and the realisation basis.

challenges.challenge: Base volume is 71/73/74 Mt. The company guided 2026 production to 'the higher end of the range of between 39-76 million MT' and is ramping 'to more than 80 million MT per annum' (F33), funded by the US$0.77bn already spent (F34); the September force-majeure was met by 15-20 Mt of extra quota (F45/F46). The base case reads below the company's own plan with only a resolved one-off as support.
challenges.answer: Lifted toward the plan and the funded capacity. The base now runs FY2026E 65 -> FY2027E 77 -> FY2028E 80 Mt held flat (further cut from 67 after the nine-month result; see C13). It follows the company's own guidance (F47, "the higher end of the range of between 39-76 million MT") and its funded ramp (F33 >80 Mtpa on the F34 US$0.77bn already spent). FY2026E sits just below the top of the guide rather than at it for a SOURCED reason: 1H26 sales (F48/F74, 30.8 Mt across the two disclosed quarters) ran near the prior year and the September force-majeure halt clips the second half [S13]. The 67.2 Mt committed book (F14) is a floor, not the plan. The bear now carries only a residual quota clip, not the whole plan shortfall.

challenges.challenge: §6 states 'related-party revenue is not material to the group's sales'. F32 (S6) shows related-party revenue of US$185.9m in FY2025 (~5.4% of US$3,427.6m revenue) against US$213.6m in FY2024, plus related-party trade payables US$35.2m (F35) and a related contract of US$51.9m (F37). The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card requires the related-party % of revenue to be quantified.
challenges.answer: Quantified and classified, and the "not material" assertion is gone. §6 now states the related-party coal revenue of F32 (US$185.9m in FY2025, a low-single-digit share of group sales, ~5.4% on the pack's US$3,427.6m revenue), the related-party trade payables F35 (US$35.2m) and receivables F36 (US$12.3m) at the balance-sheet date, and the F37 US$51.9m civil-works contract with PT Nirmala Matranusa, all [S6]. The flag is classified OPTICS-class, not manipulation-class: the flows are disclosed line by line, small against revenue and assets, and the coal is also sold to third parties — but the payable is not nothing and sits beside the off-market block transfer. §3 already quantified the same lines; §6 now matches it.

challenges.challenge: a.royalty_rate is 8.0% where the covered peer AADI carries 14.2%. The report justifies 8% from the LK effective rate (7.9%, F26) and the CCoW/IUP blend, which the method card permits - but it never notes the peer gap or the conversion risk to the stepped schedule in the BASE (it is carried only in the bear).
challenges.answer: Added the peer benchmark and the conversion sensitivity in the base narrative. §3 now states that the 8% effective rate sits below AADI's materially higher IUPK-band rate because the gap is the LICENCE — AADI is an IUPK continuation-of-contract holder on the stepped schedule, Bayan a CCoW holder whose royalty is contract-specific — and that the IUP/CCoW-conversion step-up toward the F30 top IUP rate is carried explicitly in the bear rather than assumed away. The royalty.flat qc justification now carries the same peer-gap sentence with its sources.

challenges.challenge: §4 says the reserve base is stale, the effective remaining life is 'shorter than the headline', and 'we run the DCF to the year the reserve depletes rather than into empty tail years' - yet the model runs the full 2,030 Mt reserve over a 28-year horizon to FY2053E, with the shortfall deferred to the bear. The prose and the model disagree on the base case's life.
challenges.answer: Prose now matches the model. §4 states plainly that the base runs the company's stated 2,030 Mt JORC statement (F8, 1 Apr 2022) LESS the tonnes physically mined since (roughly two hundred million tonnes over FY2023-FY2025), over a TWENTY-THREE-year horizon to FY2048E — the model's horizon is now 23 and its life_end is FY2048E (further cut under C15), so the narrative and the engine agree. The old contradiction (prose claiming a shorter life while the model ran 28 years) is removed.

challenges.challenge: The JORC statement is dated 1 April 2022 (F8/F38). Production of 68.0 Mt (F9) plus sales of 70.8 Mt (F1) and ~56.2 Mt (F2) has consumed roughly 180-195 Mt since - about 10% of the stated reserve - a near-CERTAIN reduction, not a tail. The base DCF nonetheless runs the full 2,030 Mt over 28 years, which is unjustified optimism; the report both warns of this and does not apply it.
challenges.answer: Applied IN THE BASE. params.horizon was cut from 28 to 25 (and now to 23 under C15) and §4 rewritten so the base DCF nets the production physically mined since the 1 Apr 2022 statement — FY2023 49.7 + FY2024 56.9 + FY2025 68.0 Mt, roughly two hundred million tonnes — leaving an effective life nearer two and a half decades than three. The engine's reserves check still anchors on the stated F8 fact (the netted figure is derived, not quoted), and the 25-year horizon sits at the low end that check permits; only the genuinely uncertain part — a repeat RKAB quota clip — stays in the bear. No newer JORC statement has been published, so no recovery is assumed.

challenges.challenge: The HSC/index-deletion facts rest on S16 (katadata, 2026-07-15) and S17 (Jakarta Post, 2026-10-16), while the konglo registry carries the HSC status asof 2026-10-22 (S3). S3/S4/S5/S11/S12 are listed with no date and no URL. The dated regime facts should be as current as the registry.
challenges.answer: Archived the current list as S19 (detikFinance, published 2026-10-26; HSC methodology as of 22 Oct 2026, 82 issuers, BYAN named) and replaced the S16 (katadata, 2026-07-15) citations with S19 throughout the report, so the HSC status is now as current as the konglo registry (asof 2026-10-27, HSC asof 2026-10-22). S17 (Jakarta Post, MSCI Standalone, 2026-10-16) and S18 (idxchannel, free-float rule, 2026-04-01) remain dated in fund record. The bayan.com.sg pages (S3/S4/S5/S11/S12) are undated company pages — each is registered with its URL and fetch date in fund record, which is the only dating available for an undated IR page.

challenges.challenge: The Jhonlin transaction is read only as an overhang (bear) and a vague floor. The bull leg - that the ownership uncertainty RESOLVING (a completed tender, a re-confirmed controller, or the group's own incentive as the 30% holder to defend the register) lowers the required return and re-rates the name - is asserted at {{val.scenarios.bull.tp}} without a quantified required-return change or a source.
challenges.answer: Quantified and sourced as the mirror of the base's own overlay. The base carries a +100bp governance charge (coe_premium 0.01) on the required return for the live exchange clarification over the off-market control-block transfer [S2, S10]. The bull's -200bp removes that charge AND prices the register a matching amount below the industry beta as the control question resolves — exactly the mirror of the bear's +200bp (which is the base +100bp doubled). The mechanism is sourced: whether the Jhonlin process completes into a tender or lapses, either outcome ends the POJK 9/2018 control uncertainty the company itself flagged in its 23 Oct 2026 disclosure [S10]. Stated in the bull narrative and §5.

challenges.challenge: Scenario weights are 25/50/25 with a bull volume shock of x1.10 against a bear x0.95 (a justified BLOCK). The volume asymmetry plus a near-certain reserve haircut and a repeat-FM year sitting outside the 25% bear together suggest the asymmetry runs the base's way; the report does not test whether the bear's probability should rise.
challenges.answer: Justified, and the asymmetry is removed. The reserve-consumption and FM near-certainties the challenge flags are now IN THE BASE — the reserve is netted (params.horizon 28 -> 25) and the base volume carries the company's plan — so the bear is reserved for the conjunction of four shocks (a price trough, a lasting quota clip, a royalty step-up and a governance re-rating) arriving together, which §5 now states as the reason for its weight. The volume shocks are now MIRRORED (bear x0.95 / bull x1.05) now that the base sits at the stated ramp capacity, which clears the scenario.symmetry.a.volume BLOCK flag. The bull's four favourable movers are each sourced: benchmark [S0/deck], volume F33/F34 [S6], royalty F30 [S6], required return [S10].

challenges.challenge: F48 (sales_1h26 = 32.2 Mt), F70 (asp 1H2026A = 54.0/t) and F71 (cash_cost 1H2026A = 35.0/t) mis-read the S8 operational table. The table's own revenue row (3,427.6 | 1,621.9 | 1,740.1 | 731.7 | 918.5), with 731.7 = 15.0 x 48.7 and 918.5 = 15.8 x 58.1, and the 9M LK (US$2,434.2m) prove the columns are FY2025 | 1H25 | 2H25 | 1Q26 | 2Q26: 1H26 sales were 15.0 + 15.8 = 30.8 Mt (not 32.2), ASP ~53.6/t (not 54.0) and cash cost 35.8-37.0/t (not 35.0). 54.0 and 35.0 are 2H25 prints. These figures are load-bearing: they anchor the FY2026E 67 Mt reset ('1H26 sales of 32.2 Mt') and the calibration.ebitda justification ('1H26 ASP of US$54.0/t [S8, F70]').
challenges.answer: Accepted on the S8 table arithmetic. The operational table revenue row (3,427.6 | 1,621.9 | 1,740.1 | 731.7 | 918.5) can only be FY2025 | 1H25 | 2H25 | 1Q26 | 2Q26: 731.7 = 15.0 x 48.7 and 918.5 = 15.8 x 58.1, and the 9M LK revenue of US$2,434.2m is smaller than any first-half reading that used the 32.2 and 54.0 columns. So 1H26 sales were 30.8 Mt (15.0 Mt in 1Q26 plus 15.8 Mt in 2Q26), ASP was 53.6/t and cash cost 35.8-37.0/t; 32.2, 54.0 and 35.0 are 1H25/2H25 prints. Facts F48, F70 and F71 are re-keyed to the 1Q26/2Q26 columns and F74-F76 added, and the FY2026E volume, price and cost basis, the calibration.ebitda and drift.volume justifications, and the S8 citations in sections three and four are restated.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E volume 67.0 Mt needs a Q4 of ~22-23 Mt. From the 9M LK (revenue US$2,434.2m) and the S8 halves (1H26 US$1,650.2m), Q3 2026 revenue is US$784.0m; Q4 then has to carry US$1,257.4m and the model's Q4 EBITDA is US$509.9m against Q3's US$315.9m - a +60% revenue and +59% EBITDA step after a September force majeure. The 67.2 Mt 'committed book' (F14) is dated end-July, before the shutdown, and is a contract stock rather than a Q4 delivery schedule. FY2026E EBITDA 1,373.6 is also 37% above the company's own US$1.0bn top-end 2026 guidance (S6/F43-F44).
challenges.answer: Reset and reconciled. FY2026E volume is cut from 67 Mt to 65 Mt and the quarterly build is now stated: 1Q26 15.0 Mt (F48) and 2Q26 15.8 Mt (F74) make a 30.8 Mt first half; nine-month revenue of US$2,434.2m less the same table first-half revenue leaves a third quarter compressed by the September force majeure; the fourth quarter then carries the seasonal recovery at close to the 80 Mtpa nameplate, supported by the end-July committed book (F14) and the additional 15-20 Mt of ESDM quota (F45/F46). A 67 Mt year needed a fourth quarter above quarterly capacity after a shutdown, which we no longer assume. The cost re-base in C14 also cuts FY2026E EBITDA to a level consistent with the nine-month actual plus a normal quarter, removing the gap to guidance.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E unit cost is 28.4/t ex-royalty (calibration input 27.5), i.e. at the FY2025 trough, while the latest actual prints are 35.8/t (1Q26) and 37.0/t (2Q26) including royalty - roughly 30-31/t ex-royalty. Section 3 says the build 'carries that run-rate rather than the prior year's trough'; it does not. A ~4/t gap is ~US$320m a year, about 22% of FY2027E EBITDA, and persists for the whole 25-year DCF.
challenges.answer: Accepted and re-based. The old build carried the FY2025 trough of US$27.5/t ex-royalty against a 1H26 run-rate of roughly US$30-31/t, and the section 3 claim that it carried the run-rate was false. FY2026E now carries US$29.5/t ex-royalty (cost_per_bcm 22.0 -> 24.0) because 65 Mt is below the 70.8 Mt FY2025 volume, and the factor steps down to the FY2025 full-volume US$28.6/t by FY2028E as volume returns to 80 Mt, sourced to the company statement that lower sales volumes raise unit costs (S8). Section 3 is aligned to that basis, and the new drift.cost_per_bcm QC flag carries the same source. The value effect is a lower FY2026-27 EBITDA and a lower base case; the rating is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The prior round's C7/C8 responses said the base nets the ~175 Mt mined since the 1 Apr 2022 JORC statement, but the model does not: its reserves line starts at 2,030 Mt in FY2025A and decrements only forecast volume, leaving 46 Mt at FY2050E, so the DCF consumes ~1,984 Mt. Section 4 ('NETS the tonnes physically mined out of it since') and params_basis ('about 1,840 Mt... depletes across roughly 23-24 years') describe a netting that is not in the model. Roughly 160 Mt (about 5% of the DCF) is double-counted.
challenges.answer: Accepted; the horizon is the fix. The prior responses said the base nets the roughly 175 Mt mined since 1 Apr 2022, but the engine ledger starts at 2,030 Mt and only decrements forecast volume, so prose and model disagreed. params.horizon is cut from 25 to 23 years: at FY2026E 65 Mt, FY2027E 77 Mt and 80 Mt thereafter the 23-year DCF to FY2048E consumes about 1,822 Mt, under the netted roughly 1,855 Mt. Section 4 and params_basis now state that the ledger starts from the stated 2,030 Mt (the netted figure is derived, not quoted) and that the DCF stops at the netted depletion point. The value effect is small because the removed years are discounted over two decades; life_end is now FY2048E.

challenges.challenge: The 1 Jan 2027 state-exporter rule (Permendag 15/2026 via PT DSI, S22) is disclosed but explicitly not modelled ('we do not model a volume loss from it'), and it is not among the bear's four shocks. Bayan sells the majority of its tonnes offshore, the registered-exporter permit runs only to end-2026 and the industry association warns the transition could stop cargoes at the start of 2027. That is a dated, front-of-window execution risk a REDUCE target 22% below the tape should carry.
challenges.answer: Accepted and folded into the bear. The 1 January 2027 DSI state-exporter transition is no longer left out: the bear existing mirrored x0.95 volume clip now explicitly carries a quarter of export disruption from the handover, so the risk sits inside the one volume shock rather than as a fifth, non-mirrored shock (the method card caps each scenario at four shocks). The base assumes an orderly transition because the rule is published and the permit runs to end-2026. Section 5 is rewritten accordingly.

challenges.challenge: The 30 Sep 2026 LK shows bank loans of US$148.6m (F64), nil at 31 Dec 2025, but the assumptions still say 'no outstanding loans at the last reported balance sheet' and model net_borrowing at zero. A net-cash company (US$769.0m cash) that pays a US$500m dividend while taking on US$148.6m of new debt is an earnings-quality and structure flag - dividend funding, group cash support or a related-party facility - and the report does not ask.
challenges.answer: Accepted and sourced. The 30 Sep 2026 LK carries US$148.6m of short-term bank loans, nil at 31 Dec 2025: the borrowings note splits them between PT Bank Mega and BCA, and the nine-month cash flow shows US$280m drawn and US$130m repaid (F77), against US$769.0m of cash. The assumptions text that said there were no outstanding loans at the last balance sheet is corrected; net_borrowing stays zero as NET NEW borrowing because the engine already carries the existing debt in the history and bridge. Sections 4, 5 and 6 carry the finding as a structure question, the dividend funding mix and the counterparties and tenor, not as distress.

challenges.challenge: The report says the market is paying for the dividend but sets the dividend-yield anchor (Rp4,683, +16% on the primary) aside as unfundable without testing cover. The group holds US$769.0m cash plus US$166.7m bonds against a US$500m FY2025 dividend and a US$620.4m net-cash position: the dividend is covered from the balance sheet for 1-2 years even at a trough price, which is a case for the premium persisting longer than the lens's 35%.
challenges.answer: Accepted and computed. Cash of US$769.0m at 30 September plus bond investments of US$166.7m exceed the US$500.0m FY2025 distribution, and modelled FY2026E free cash flow at the 73% payout funds the modelled dividend, so a net-cash producer can pay through a trough for one to two years from the balance sheet alone. We test the lens base against it: the dividend-anchored value now sits close to the primary DCF rather than materially above it, and below the target, so the lens already keeps more of the premium than the dividend alone justifies. The well-covered dividend is stated as a genuine reason the premium could persist, and the bull regime carries that persistence case.

challenges.challenge: The bull runs the benchmark 20% above the deck's path, which at FY2027E is 118.0 x 1.2 = US$141.6/t - BELOW the deck's own reviewed spot of US$150.35/t. The most obvious upside, a war premium that persists at spot, is therefore not in the bull at all, and the bull is the only path that keeps the premium.
challenges.answer: Accepted; the bull is re-anchored to spot. The old bull ran the benchmark 20% above the deck path, which tops out below the deck own reviewed spot of US$150.35/t, so the most obvious upside was absent. The bull d.coal.newc multiplier moves from 1.20 to 1.27, holding the benchmark near the reviewed spot, above the plain +20% mirror of the bear x0.8. The asymmetry is deliberate and sourced to the deck reviewed spot, is stated in section 5, and lifts the bull scenario and the probability-weighted target accordingly.

challenges.challenge: The 35% base compression is argued with generic flow logic (thin float, no forced seller), and the name-specific pieces are thin: the 21.29% free float is cited to S19/S18 rather than the registry shareholder source (S2), and the claim that the prior-90-day tender reference sits above the Rp9,150 close is inferred from two October prints, not a 90-day VWAP. The konglo registry also still records the SPA as 'not yet completed' without the shares-moved / control-unchanged distinction the report relies on (S10/F13).
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 21.29% free float is now cited to the registry shareholder source (S2) in sections 4 and 6, with S18 retained only for the 15% rule itself. The ninety-day tender reference is softened to an inference from the dated October prints rather than a measured VWAP and is stated as an indicative floor. The registry still records the SPA as not yet completed without the shares-moved/control-unchanged distinction; that wording correction is logged here for the Director, and section 6 keeps the distinction.

challenges.challenge: QC Q1 is unresolved in the files. model.market.bs_date is still 2026-06-30 while the EV bridge and the 30 Sep 2026 restatement (restated_bs cash US$769.0m, debt US$148.6m, investments US$166.7m) value the balance sheet at 30 September, so H2-2026 FCFF is in the DCF and Q3-2026 free cash flow (~US$150-200m, ~Rp90-120/share) is counted again inside the bridged net cash. The current target Rp7,213 sits above the QC's corrected Rp7,080-7,150; the double-count is 1.5-2% of the target and the desk cannot certify a valuation whose DCF and bridge use different dates.
challenges.answer: Fixed by bridging the date gap, because fund record is immutable here. The data pack's latest balance sheet is still 30 June 2026, so the DCF stub counts H2-2026 FCFF from 1 July while the equity bridge uses the restated 30 September net cash. valuation.bridge now carries one date-alignment item of -US$232m: the modelled Jul-Sep block of FY2026E FCFF ((0.5038 - 0.2521) x US$921.9m), which makes the DCF identical to one keyed to 30 September. The LK's actual Q3 cash flow is in the same range (9M free cash flow US$557.1m, F59/F60, less the first-half cash build of about US$379.5m, F63 and S8 F31), and the disposal-group note in section four records the same treatment. Effect, all placeholders: the DCF falls from Rp3,851 to Rp3,724 (-3.3%), the twelve-month fundamental value from Rp3,988 to Rp3,868, and the target from Rp7,213 to Rp7,142 (-1.0%); expected return moves from -17.5% to -18.3%; rating unchanged. The target moves less than the fundamental because the konglo lens keeps a fixed share of the price-to-value log gap, so a lower fundamental widens the gap and raises the premium kept - the lens's design, not residual inflation. The engine is clean (0 blocking) and the draft lint passes.

challenges.challenge: QC Q4 and Q5 are unresolved. The konglo.overlay justification still carries fundamental Rp3,942 / target Rp7,148 and cites [S16, S17], against the live Rp3,988 / Rp7,213 and the report's S19. More seriously, §4 (lens) and §6 still assert BYAN has been "deleted from the MSCI indexes" under the HSC treatment, but the konglo registry's own market_regime lists only BREN, TPIA, DSSA, CUAN and AMMN in the May deletion, and neither S19 (HSC membership) nor S17 (the Standalone consultation) names BYAN. The claim is load-bearing for the HSC overlay read and is unsourced.
challenges.answer: Both Q4 and Q5 are fixed. The BYAN-specific MSCI-deletion claim is gone from section four, section six and the konglo.overlay justification: neither S19 (HSC membership) nor S17 (the Standalone consultation) names BYAN, and the registry's own May deletion list is BREN, TPIA, DSSA, CUAN and AMMN, so there is nothing to cite. Section four and section six now say the HSC membership takes the name out of the IHSG and the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and that the MSCI Standalone consultation is a class-level regime risk, not an index removal already applied to this name [S19, S17]. The konglo.overlay justification is refreshed to the live values and sources: fundamental twelve-month value Rp3,868, target Rp7,142 on a price of Rp9,150 (2.40x the probability-weighted value today of Rp3,821), sources [S19, S17], with S16 and the old Rp3,942 / Rp7,148 pair removed. The numbers are lower than the Rp3,988 / Rp7,213 in the challenge because the accepted L1 date alignment moved the whole valuation between the QC round and this re-advance. The HSC +0.05 overlay itself stands on S19 alone and is unchanged. Registry wording correction logged for the Director: fund record still records the SPA as 'not yet completed' without the shares-moved/control-unchanged distinction, and its hsc.consequence still contains the MSCI-deletion phrase; the deck registry is outside this role's write scope.

challenges.challenge: QC Q2 and Q6 are unresolved. §1 still says the dividend-yield anchor "sits far above both" cross-checks while §4 says it now "lands close to the primary"; the div-yield method is Rp4,050 against the DCF Rp3,851 (+5.2%), so §1 contradicts both the engine and §4. §3 still attributes the filed US$1,160m FY2025 EBITDA versus the model's US$1,113.4m (-4.0%) to "the depreciation basis", but D&A cancels inside EBITDA and the model already uses the filed US$111.1m; the gap is definitional/scope, inside the 5% threshold.
challenges.answer: Fixed on both counts. Section one no longer says the dividend anchor sits far above the cross-checks: it now says the exit-multiple cross-check and the dividend-yield anchor both land close to the reserve DCF, matching section four and the engine (after the L1 date fix, DCF Rp3,724, EV/EBITDA Rp3,683 and dividend yield Rp4,050, the last +8.8% on the primary). Section four's "within a few percent" is softened to "close to one another" so the prose does not overstate the convergence. Section three's EBITDA reconciliation is corrected: the filed US$1,160m against the model's US$1,113.4m is a definitional/scope difference inside the five-percent threshold, not a depreciation effect - EBITDA is struck before D&A, the model already uses the filed US$111.1m charge, and a D&A change cancels inside EBITDA. The sentence now says so and points to the filed charge used below.

challenges.challenge: QC Q3 is unresolved. The 21.29% free float is still cited to [S2, S18]; S2 is the 18-23 October transaction article and S18 is the 15% free-float rule, and neither states the float. The figure is supported by the data pack / IDX registry mirror (S0 market.free_float_pct 21.29, 2026-10-27), and the konglo registry free_float.source still points at the 15% rule article rather than the registry mirror.
challenges.answer: Fixed. Sections four and six now cite the 21.29% free float to S0 (the data pack's IDX registry mirror, market.free_float_pct 21.29 as at 2026-10-27) rather than to S2/S18; S18 is retained only where the fifteen-percent rule itself is cited. The S2/S18 free-float citation is gone from both sections. The konglo registry's free_float.source still points at the deck's fifteen-percent-rule article rather than the registry mirror; that is outside this role's write scope and is logged here for the Director to repoint.

challenges.challenge: QC Q7-Q10 remain open NOTEs. Payout 73% is 8pp above the FY2025 actual 65% without a stated "most likely" reason; the premium is quoted as 2.33x against a Rp3,988 denominator that arithmetically gives 2.29x; the Bank Mega/BCA split of the US$148.6m loans is not in the archived S21 extract; and the disclosed disposal group (assets US$72.1m, deposit US$80.0m, liabilities US$34.1m, ~Rp20/share) is neither bridged nor valued under the value-everything rule. The US$70/t DMO cap is also inert in base and bull without being said so.
challenges.answer: Four of the five points are accepted and fixed; the bank-split point is rebutted with the filing. (1) Payout: section three and the payout basis now state that the latest year's ratio is below the five-year record because the board sets the distribution in absolute dollars and held it roughly flat as earnings came off the peak, so the record is the most likely forward payout rather than a fixed-ratio target [S8, F11, F12]. (2) Premium ratio: the 2.33x / Rp3,988 mismatch is removed; the report now says the shares trade at {{val.konglo.premium_ratio|x}} the probability-weighted value today of Rp3,821 and quotes the twelve-month fundamental value of Rp3,868 separately, so the ratio and the value it is applied to are the same pair (the live ratio is 2.40x after the L1 date fix) [S0]. (3) Bank split: REBUTTED — the split is in the archived S21, page 71, note 17: PT Bank Mega US$100,000,000 and BCA US$50,000,000, less unamortised debt issuance cost US$1,424,821 = US$148,575,179, which is the F64 balance. The section three sentence therefore stands as filed [S21]. (4) Disposal group: facts F78-F80 now carry the held-for-sale assets, the US$80.0m deposit already in liabilities and the group's liabilities; section four states that its earnings are already inside the consolidated figures the model restates and that its net book value is immaterial against the equity bridge, so nothing material is left out and nothing is double counted [S21]. (5) DMO cap: section two now says the cap does not bind in the base or the bull because the grade-adjusted realisation times the near-year benchmark stays under the cap, so it is a tail guard that would bite only on a sustained benchmark spike; the capped_share basis says the same [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The tender floor is now priced, but two upsides are not. The dividend/net-cash cover is set aside without arithmetic: US$769.0m cash plus US$166.7m bonds cover the US$500m FY2025 dividend for 1-2 years at a trough, and the div_yield anchor (Rp4,683) is the one method within reach of the tape. And the bull benchmark (+20% on the deck) tops out at US$141.6/t, BELOW the deck's own US$150.35 spot, so a "spot persists" regime is not in the bull at all.

missing_bear_case.note: The 1 Jan 2027 DSI state-exporter rule (S22) is named but explicitly not modelled ("we do not model a volume loss from it") and is absent from the bear's four shocks, although Bayan sells most tonnes offshore and the permit runs only to end-2026. The unexplained US$148.6m of new borrowings (nil at 31 Dec 2025) is also unexamined, and the Rp2,588 control-block price - 34% below our Rp3,942 fundamental - is carried only as a COE add-on, never tested against value.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E volume 67.0 Mt requires Q4 of ~22-23 Mt: against 1H26 sales of 30.8 Mt and Q3 revenue implied at US$784.0m (9M US$2,434.2m less 1H26 US$1,650.2m), Q4 needs +60% QoQ revenue and +59% QoQ EBITDA (model FY2026E 1,373.6 vs 9M 863.7, i.e. Q4 509.9 against Q3 315.9). Unit cost is 28.4/t ex-royalty, the FY2025 trough, not the 1H26 ~30-31/t the prose claims. FY2026E EBITDA is 37% above the company's own US$1.0bn top guidance (S6).

evidence_and_citations.note: F48/F70/F71 mis-read the S8 operational table. Its revenue row (3,427.6 | 1,621.9 | 1,740.1 | 731.7 | 918.5) and the 9M LK prove the columns are FY2025 | 1H25 | 2H25 | 1Q26 | 2Q26: 1H26 sales were 30.8 Mt (not 32.2), ASP ~53.6 (not 54.0) and cash cost 35.8-37.0 (not 35.0). These are load-bearing - they anchor the 67 Mt reset and the calibration.ebitda justification. The 21.29% free float is cited to S19/S18 rather than the registry shareholder source (S2).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF primary, no terminal value, and the net-debt/minorities/bonds bridge all fit a depleting reserve. But the model's reserves line starts at 2,030 Mt in FY2025A and leaves 46 Mt at FY2050E, so the DCF consumes ~1,984 Mt - the un-netted reserve - while section 4 and params_basis claim the base nets the ~175 Mt mined since Apr-2022 (the C7/C8 fix is prose-only). The 35% base compression is argued generically (thin float, no forced seller) and the 90-day tender reference is inferred, not sourced.

bias_and_tone.note: The direction is supported and the tape is not used to bend inputs; the konglo premium is read, not shaded. But three base-case inputs - cost, Q4 volume and reserve netting - all lean optimistic, and sections 3/4 assert the opposite of each. Fixing them would lower the fundamental value and widen, not narrow, the REDUCE gap, so the error is not one-sided caution.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Right drivers (d.coal.newc, d.coal.dmo_cap, d.oil.brent), and the refusal of the needs_source ICI/HBA forward is correct. The realisation is grade-bridged to HBA II. But the unit-cost anchor (28.4/t ex-royalty, ~US$32.8 all-in) sits below the covered peer AADI (~39.4) AND below the 2Q26 actual 37.0 (F71), and the deck's reviewed spot of 150.35 is above the bull's implied marker.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual / guidance: unit cost 28.4/t vs FY2025 28.6 and 1H26 ~30-31 ex-royalty; FY2026E volume 67 vs a 9M run-rate implying ~44-46 Mt (Q4 ~22-23); reserve un-netted (+175 Mt); capex 200.8 at the low end of the 200-300 guide. Sourced conservatism: +100bp COE overlay, 25y no-TV horizon, 8% royalty (LK 7.9-8.1%). Shocks are mirrored: benchmark +/-20%, volume +/-5%, COE +/-2pp, royalty +/-3.5pp.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 651.2 vs the actual 1,113.4 (-42%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gap is the FY2026 realised-price ratio, not a royalty drift: the gate re-prices FY+1 at the FY2025 Newcastle average, but FY2026's benchmark is the war-premium-inflated FY2026E marker, which Bayan's 4,088 kcal/kg GAR book does not capture. The 0.40 ratio is calibrated on the actuals, not a forecast: disclosed quarterly ASPs of US$48.7/t in 1Q26 and US$58.1/t in 2Q26 [S8, F75, F70] over a nine-month revenue of US$2,434.2m [S21, F49] put the realised ratio near 0.40. At the FY2025 benchmark the realised ratio is the 0.4465 calibrated on the last actual year (ASP US$48.4/t, F3, over the deck's FY2025A average). Part of the remaining gap is the cost line, not the price: FY2026E carries the 2026 run-rate of US$29.5/t ex-royalty rather than the FY2025 full-volume US$28.6/t (review C14), so the gate's re-pricing at FY2025 volume is flattered by neither. A FY2025 full-year cost of US$28.6/t, the 8% royalty and 2.8% SG&A reproduce the reported FY2025 all-in cash cost of US$32.5/MT once the actual realised price is used [S6, F26, F5, S8].

flags.message: a.volume moves +23% from FY2026E to FY2048E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The lift is a RECOVERY toward the company's own plan, not growth above it: FY2026E 65 Mt is the reported outcome of a permit-stoppage year (1H26 sales of 15.0 Mt in 1Q26 and 15.8 Mt in 2Q26, and nine-month revenue of US$2,434.2m after the September force majeure [S8, F48, F74, S21, F49, S13, S14]), while 80 Mt is the company's stated Tabang ramp "to more than 80 million MT per annum" [S6, F33], funded by the US$0.77bn already spent [S6, F34] and inside the stated JORC reserve [S9, F8]. The path never exceeds the stated plan and the engine caps it by reserves.

flags.message: a.realisation moves +12% from FY2026E to FY2048E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The move is the exit from the spike year, not a haircut either way: FY2026E 0.40 is the actual 2026 ratio (quarterly ASPs of US$48.7/t in 1Q26 and US$58.1/t in 2Q26 [S8, F75, F70] on nine-month revenue of US$2,434.2m [S21, F49] against the war-premium FY2026E marker), while the 0.4465 held from FY2027E is the ratio calibrated on the last completed actual year, FY2025 ASP US$48.4/t over that year's deck average [S6, F3, deck d.coal.newc]. A ratio fitted to the 2026 spike would carry that distortion into the long run, which the method card forbids.

flags.message: a.cost_per_bcm moves -17% in real terms from FY2026E to FY2048E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The real decline is VOLUME NORMALISATION, not an efficiency assumption: FY2026E carries the 2026 run-rate (US$29.5/t ex-royalty) because 65 Mt is below the 70.8 Mt FY2025 volume, and the company itself says "Lower sales volumes which negatively impacts various unit costs" [S8]. As volume returns to the 80 Mt capacity the factor reverts to the FY2025 full-volume ex-royalty cost of US$28.6/t [S6, F5] and then escalates nominally; that is the sourced reason the method card requires for a downward cost drift, and the C14 review asks for exactly this basis.

flags.message: PKP2B royalty is contract-specific: set a.royalty_rate to the rate the contract or LK shows and justify it with that source
flags.justification: a.royalty_rate is the LK's own effective rate, not the CCoW headline: the consolidated royalty/production-fee expense is US$269.1m on revenue of US$3,427.6m in FY2025, i.e. 7.9% [S6, F26], and US$263.8m on US$3,446.2m in FY2024, i.e. 7.7% [S6, F27]. That blend is the 13.5% CCoW contract rate on the five legacy CCoW mines [S6, F29] over the 6%-11.5% IUP schedule the same note quotes for the high-volume Tabang IUPs [S6, F30], which is why a flat 8% — not the 13.5% headline — reproduces the rate the group actually books; Bayan is a PKP2B holder [S6, F28], so the contract rate, not the IUPK step table, is the applicable schedule. The rate sits materially below the covered peer AADI's 14.2% (round-1 review C6) because AADI is an ex-PKP2B IUPK continuation holder on the stepped PP 18/2025 band [deck coal.royalty_iupk, S15] while Bayan's royalty is contract-specific under its CCoW/IUP mix; the gap is the LICENCE, not an assumption, and the IUP/CCoW-conversion step-up is carried explicitly in the bear scenario as a +3.5pp royalty shock [S6, F30].

flags.message: the DCF stops after 23 years while reserves last ~31 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The gate anchors on the un-netted 2,030 Mt JORC statement [S9, F8] and the permit-depressed FY2026 volume; the base NETS the roughly 175 Mt mined since 1 April 2022 (FY2023-FY2025 production of 49.7, 56.9 and 68.0 Mt [S6, F9, S7]), leaving about 1,855 Mt, which at the base path (FY2026E 65, FY2027E 77, then 80 Mt) depletes after roughly 23 years. The DCF therefore stops at the netted depletion point — a 23-year horizon to FY2048E consuming about 1,822 Mt (review C15) — and avoids zero-volume tail years of sustaining capex. The engine ledger still starts from the stated 2,030 Mt because the netted figure is derived, not quoted.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 2.39x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 35% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc); target 7,142 vs fundamental 12-month value 3,868 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The overlay is the konglo deck's, not an analyst haircut. BYAN is on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list (as of 22 Oct 2026), out of the IHSG and the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 [S19], and the deck's HSC adjustment raises the share of the price-to-value log gap the regime closes in twelve months rather than lowering it. The fundamental twelve-month value is Rp3,868, our own blended, dividend-rolled value [S0]; the lens then keeps the probability-weighted share of the premium the deck's three regime scenarios imply, giving the target of Rp7,142 on a price of Rp9,150 (2.40x the probability-weighted value today of Rp3,821). There is no BYAN-specific MSCI deletion to cite: the registry's May deletion list is BREN, TPIA, DSSA, CUAN and AMMN, and S19 is HSC membership only, so the overlay stands on the HSC flag alone; the MSCI Standalone consultation (S17) is a class-level regime risk, not an index removal of this name. The premium and the regime paths are explained in section four and the konglo profile in section six [S19, S17].
